title: End to end: an escalation resolved by another holder, seen on the timeline and the overview

story.i_want_to: see one real item escalated by one holder, refused to that holder, re-queued by another and delivered, against the sandbox repo
story.so_that: release 5's promise that nothing waits for me is proven on the deployed system, not only in unit tests

rationale: PRD R4's end-to-end path is 'an escalation resolved by another holder'. Unit and ConnCase tests prove each guard in isolation; only a run through the real API, a real runner and the sandbox repo proves the pieces compose: the holder credential, the escalation event's actor, the self guard, the holder edge, placement and the merge gate. This story extends the end-to-end suite release 2 created rather than adding a second harness.

acceptance_criteria.description: A new scenario in the end-to-end suite registers two holders A and B through holder_register, opens a sandbox issue, and waits (bounded, 15 minutes) for the item to reach claimed with A's holder as the claim's holder.
A escalates the item through escalate_story with a reason; the scenario asserts the item is at escalated and the timeline's newest transition names A's holder_id as actor.
A's own resolve_escalation(to: queued) answers 409 self_resolve_blocked, and the item is still at escalated with an unchanged stage row.
B's resolve_escalation(to: queued) answers 200; the item then reaches done (bounded, 30 minutes) through placement, review, merge and verify on the sandbox repo, with a merged sandbox PR.
work_item_timeline for the item lists, in order, A's escalation, B's holder_resolution and the transition into done, each with its actor and a non-empty reason.
factory_overview for the sandbox project counts the item in throughput done for window_days 1, and its waiting.escalated holds no item of this run.
The scenario cleans up whatever it created even when it fails (closes the sandbox issue and PR, revokes both holder credentials), and a failure prints the item's full timeline.

test_cases.name: mix e2e --only escalation_other_holder against the sandbox
preconditions: deployed loopctl with release 5; sandbox mkreyman/loopctl-e2e-sandbox enrolled; at least one live runner
expected_results: the item is done, the self resolve was refused, the timeline and overview assertions pass

test_cases.name: a forced failure still cleans up and prints the timeline
preconditions: the scenario with an injected failing assertion after the escalation step (E2E_FAIL_AT=after_escalate)
steps: list open sandbox issues and the run's holder keys
expected_results: scenario fails with the timeline printed; no open issue or live key of this run remains

test_cases.name: the self guard holds against the deployed API (curl step inside the scenario)

technical_notes: Suite: the end-to-end suite (mix e2e, sandbox mkreyman/loopctl-e2e-sandbox) is provided by release 2 (README names table: end-to-end suite); add one scenario module beside its existing ones and reuse its sandbox issue, cleanup and bounded-wait helpers. Do not add a second harness.
Holders: holder_register and the holder credential are provided by release 3 (README names table: holder, holder credential).
APIs used: escalate_story (mcp-server/index.js:4954), resolve_escalation opened to holders by US-52.31, work_item_timeline (US-52.29), factory_overview (US-52.30).

The holder that claims first is not chosen by the scenario: it claims the item itself with A's credential through claim_story (lib/loopctl_web/router.ex claim route) rather than waiting for a runner, so the escalating holder is known; B's resolution then sends it to the runner pool for delivery.
Bounded waits poll the stage route every 10 s and fail with the timeline at the bound; nothing waits without a deadline.
non_goals: The sweep path (no holder acts): US-52.34's own tests; an end-to-end of the sweep would take the 30-minute grace window.
Intervention verbs end to end: covered by their ConnCase tests.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.35.4: each wait is bounded and polls; a lost answer is re-read from the stage route, never assumed.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.35.7: the scenario's own artefacts (issue, PR, holder keys) are cleaned up on success and failure, so a crashed run leaves no state for the next.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.35.7: a rerun creates its own issue and holders, so two runs never share an item.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.35.4: a delivery slower than 30 minutes fails the scenario with the timeline printed, rather than hanging the suite.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: the scenario runs as one mix process against the deployed API; it schedules nothing.

definition_of_done: mix e2e --only escalation_other_holder passes against production and the sandbox, and its run is linked in the release PR.
The sandbox repo has no open issue or PR left by the run.
defaults: Bounds: 15 minutes to claim, 30 minutes from resolution to done (owner may change).
The escalating holder claims the item itself rather than waiting for a runner, so the scenario knows who escalated.
